Methodology

Exactly what we check, how we check it, and what it does and doesn't mean. UCP profiles are our headline measure; four supporting signals are listed per store. Crawl date: 2026-10-19.

What this does and doesn't mean

  • UCP profile found: the store publishes a Universal Commerce Protocol profile at /.well-known/ucp, the machine-readable profile AI shopping agents read, and lists what it supports (for example checkout). It doesn't guarantee that any particular assistant buys from it; that depends on the assistant.
  • No UCP profile found: we found no UCP profile. It does not mean AI agents can't shop there. Agents can use a store through a normal web browser, and some agent shopping runs through channels we can't see from outside, such as product feeds shared privately with AI assistants.
  • Couldn't check: the site refused or failed our request, so we don't know either way.
  • UCP is our headline measure. We also list four supporting signals per store (section 1b), but we don't test purchases, and we don't score or rank how well a store works with any assistant.

1. What we look for

The UCP specification says platforms discover a business by fetching its business profile from /.well-known/ucp (UCP specification overview). The profile is JSON with a ucp object: protocol version, services, capabilities and payment handlers. We fetch that path on each website after reading /robots.txt. This is our headline measure. The other things we read are listed in section 1b and section 5.

1b. Supporting signals (beyond UCP)

UCP stays our headline measure and trend. Since October 2026 we also record other public signals of how a store presents itself to AI agents. Each store page lists them separately; we don't combine them into a score.

SignalHow we checkWhat it meansWhat it doesn't mean
Agent checkout profile (UCP)/.well-known/ucp (see section 1)The store publishes the machine-readable profile and lists what it supports.That any particular assistant buys from it.
Agent tools (MCP endpoint)If the UCP profile names an MCP endpoint, we send one read-only JSON-RPC tools/list request, identifying ourselves with our agent profile. We never call a tool.The endpoint is live and lists tools (for example catalog search, cart, checkout) right now.That a purchase completes without the buyer; checkouts may hand the buyer back to the store's own checkout page.
AI-agent rules in robots.txtGroups in /robots.txt that name ChatGPT-User, Claude-User, Perplexity-User, Google-Agent, OAI-SearchBot, Claude-SearchBot, PerplexityBot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot or Google-Extended, plus Content-Signal lines. Tokens from OpenAI, Anthropic, Perplexity and Google.The site's stated wishes for each kind of AI agent: user-requested, search or training.A technical block or permission. OpenAI, Perplexity and Google say their user-requested agents may not follow robots.txt; Anthropic says its bots do.
Guidance for AI assistants/llms.txt and /agents.md (Markdown files, not web pages)The site publishes instructions for AI assistants. On Shopify these are generated by the platform.That assistants read them; llms.txt is a community proposal, not a formal standard.
Product dataOne page that looks like a product page, found via a link on the home page or, failing that, at most two sitemap files. We look for schema.org Product markup with an Offer that has price, currency and availability.Product facts are machine-readable on the page.Anything about checkout. "Not checked" means we couldn't reach a product page, often because of bot protection or pages built by scripts.

We also record, without a public column until a store first publishes one, two newer discovery files: the Agentic Commerce Protocol discovery document at /.well-known/acp.json and the MCP AI catalog at /.well-known/ai-catalog.json.

We also read /.well-known/poppy.json (Personal Agent Protocol), /.well-known/agent-card.json and /.well-known/agent.json (A2A agent card), and ai-catalog.json above, record-only: no public column, and they never change a store's results.

When a site's bot protection refuses our identified crawler, its store page says so in a neutral note. That only describes how the site treated our crawler, not whether shoppers or AI agents can use it.

What we can't see from outside

A lot of agent shopping runs through channels that leave no public trace on a store's website. We never count these as "no":

  • ChatGPT product feeds: merchants share catalogs with OpenAI privately through the Agentic Commerce Protocol (OpenAI, March 2026).
  • Shopify Catalog and agentic storefronts: Shopify syndicates eligible stores to AI channels, managed in each store's admin (Shopify Help Center).
  • Microsoft Copilot Checkout enrolment (Microsoft Advertising).
  • Card-network agent programs: Visa Intelligent Commerce and its Trusted Agent Protocol, and Mastercard Agent Pay (Cloudflare).
  • Web Bot Auth: whether a store verifies signed AI agents (Cloudflare docs).

2. Who we track: three segments, side by side

  • Shopify stores (1188): Stores from public lists of Shopify stores.
  • Big retailers (380): Retailers on Wikipedia's List of largest retail companies, or with Wikipedia articles in 10+ languages.
  • Other retailers & marketplaces (708): Other retail chains, department stores, supermarkets, hypermarkets and online marketplaces listed on Wikipedia or Wikidata.

Sources: Wikipedia list pages (largest retail companies, department stores by country, supermarket chains, hypermarkets, online marketplaces) resolved to Wikidata for official websites; Wikidata queries for retail chains and e-commerce companies; and public GitHub lists of Shopify stores (ihof/shopify, dipinarora9/Shopify-Domains-Scraper, first 900 of TeamDukaan/performance). This is not a random sample of all stores; shares are shares of our list.

3. One retailer, many country sites

When a retailer's Wikidata entry lists several official websites (for example one per country), we check up to 8 of them and show them as children of one retailer. A retailer counts as publishing UCP if at least one of its sites does.

4. "Couldn't check" is not "no"

Many large retailers use bot protection that refuses automated requests. We never try to get around it. A retailer is couldn't check when every one of its sites refused us (401/403/429), timed out, failed TLS/DNS, or disallowed the path in robots.txt. These are shown separately and excluded from adoption rates. A retailer is no UCP profile only when at least one of its sites answered and had no profile.

5. How we fetch

  • User-Agent: ShopBotIndexBot/1.0 (+https://shopbotindex.com/methodology.html#crawler; hello@shopbotindex.com; reads /robots.txt, /.well-known/ucp, /.well-known/acp.json, /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, /.well-known/poppy.json, /.well-known/agent-card.json, /.well-known/agent.json, /llms.txt, /agents.md, the home page, up to 2 sitemap files and 1 product page, and sends one read-only MCP tools/list request to the endpoint a UCP profile declares) (The crawl of 2026-10-19 still used the earlier User-Agent ShopBotIndexBot/1.0 (+https://shopbotindex.com/methodology.html#crawler; hello@shopbotindex.com; reads only /robots.txt and /.well-known/ucp), which read only /robots.txt and /.well-known/ucp.)
  • What we read on each website, and nothing else: /robots.txt, /.well-known/ucp, /.well-known/acp.json, /.well-known/ai-catalog.json, /.well-known/poppy.json, /.well-known/agent-card.json, /.well-known/agent.json, /llms.txt, /agents.md, the home page, at most two sitemap files (only when the home page links no product), and one product page. When the UCP profile names an MCP endpoint, we also send it one read-only tools/list request. That's usually 10 to 14 requests per website per week, and never more than 18.
  • robots.txt is read first and respected for every one of those URLs. If /.well-known/ucp is disallowed for us, we skip the website entirely.
  • At most 12 websites at a time for the UCP pass and 16 for the extra signals, always one request at a time per website, with a pause between requests (1 second for the extra signals), 10 to 12 second timeouts, HTTPS only. If a listed host is unreachable we try the same domain with or without www.. The extra signals run within a fixed weekly time budget; websites we don't reach in time show as "not checked".
  • Site owners: to have your site excluded, disallow / (or just the paths above) for ShopBotIndexBot in robots.txt, or email hello@shopbotindex.com.

6. Site-level results this crawl (2656 websites)

  • No profile (HTTP 404 or similar): 933
  • UCP profile found: 780
  • Couldn't check: timeout, TLS or DNS error: 371
  • Couldn't check: request refused (401/403/429): 287
  • No profile (answered with a web page, not JSON): 202
  • Couldn't check: robots.txt disallows: 83

7. Platform

"Shopify" means the profile's endpoints or extensions reference Shopify. Anything else is shown as another platform. We can only identify a platform for stores that publish a profile.

8. Weekly changes

Each crawl is saved with its date. The "What changed" page compares retailer-level status with the previous crawl: joined, left, couldn't check this time (not counted as leaving), capability changes, and newly tracked retailers (not counted as joining).

9. AI assistants table

Only official company announcements and help-centre pages, linked per row. We don't test those integrations.

10. Add, remove or correct a store

Run a store or retailer that should be added, removed or corrected, or think a result is wrong? Email hello@shopbotindex.com with the store's domain. We re-check it in the next weekly crawl and never change a result by hand.
